arxiv-2012-03480.title: Meta Ordinal Regression Forest For Learning with Unsure Lung Nodules
arxiv-2012-03480.creator: \name Yiming Lei \email ymlei17@fudan.edu.cn
arxiv-2012-03480.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by \name Yiming Lei \email ymlei17@fudan.edu.cn. Deep learning-based methods have achieved promising performance in early detection and classification of lung nodules, most of which discard unsure nodules and simply deal with a binary classification— malignant vs benign . Recently, an unsure data model (UDM) was proposed to incorporate those unsure nodules by formulating this problem as an ordinal regression, showing better performance over traditional binary classification.

arxiv-2101-01164.title: Stoichiometry controls the dynamics of liquid condensates of associative proteins
arxiv-2101-01164.creator: Pierre Ronceray, Yaojun Zhang, Xichong Liu, Ned S. Wingreen
arxiv-2101-01164.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pierre Ronceray, Yaojun Zhang, Xichong Liu, Ned S. Wingreen. Multivalent associative proteins with strong complementary interactions play a crucial role in phase separation of intracellular liquid condensates. We study the internal dynamics of such “bond-network” condensates comprised of two complementary proteins via scaling analysis and molecular dynamics. We find that when stoichiometry is balanced, relaxation slows down dramatically due to a scarcity of alternative partners following a bond break.

arxiv-2101-11824.title: Exploring Lightweight Interventions at Posting Time to Reduce the Sharing of Misinformation on Social Media Journal: PACMHCI Volume: 5 CSCW1 18 4 DOI: 10.1145/3449092 CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in collaborative and social computing CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies
arxiv-2101-11824.creator: Farnaz Jahanbakhsh, Amy X. Zhang, Adam J. Berinsky, Gordon Pennycook, David G. Rand, David R. Karger
arxiv-2101-11824.description: Abstract . When users on social media share content without considering its veracity, they may unwittingly be spreading misinformation. In this work, we investigate the design of lightweight interventions that nudge users to assess the accuracy of information as they share it.

arxiv-2111-04551.title: Sexism Prediction in Spanish and English Tweets Using Monolingual and Multilingual BERT and Ensemble Models
arxiv-2111-04551.creator: Angel Felipe Magnossão de Paula, Roberto Fray da Silva, Ipek Baris Schlicht
arxiv-2111-04551.description: Abstract The popularity of social media has created problems such as hate speech and sexism. The identification and classification of sexism in social media are very relevant tasks, as they would allow building a healthier social environment. Nevertheless, these tasks are considerably challenging.

arxiv-2305-18722.creator: Andrew Weng, Everardo Olide, Iaroslav Kovalchuk, Jason B. Siegel, Anna Stefanopoulou
arxiv-2305-18722.description: Abstract This work proposes a semi-empirical model for the SEI growth process during the early stages of lithium-ion battery formation cycling and aging. By combining a full-cell model which tracks half-cell equilibrium potentials, a zero-dimensional model of SEI growth kinetics, and a semi-empirical description of cell thickness expansion, the resulting model replicated experimental trends measured on a 2.

arxiv-2307-02301.title: Sumformer: Universal Approximation for Efficient Transformers
arxiv-2307-02301.creator: Silas Alberti, Niclas Dern, Laura Thesing, Gitta Kutyniok
arxiv-2307-02301.description: Abstract Natural language processing (NLP) made an impressive jump with the introduction of Transformers. ChatGPT is one of the most famous examples, changing the perception of the possibilities of AI even outside the research community. However, besides the impressive performance, the quadratic time and space complexity of Transformers with respect to sequence length pose significant limitations for handling long sequences.

arxiv-2307-15666.title: Classifying core collapse supernova remnants by their morphology as shaped by the last exploding jets
arxiv-2307-15666.creator: Noam Soker
arxiv-2307-15666.description: Abstract Under the assumption that jets explode all core collapse supernovae (CCSNe) I classify 14 CCSN remnants (CCSNRs) into five groups according to their morphology as shaped by jets, and attribute the classes to the specific angular momentum of the pre-collapse core.

arxiv-2404-17189.title: Nonclassical Properties of a State Generated by a Driven Dispersive Interaction
arxiv-2404-17189.creator: Naveen Kumar 1, Arpita Chatterjee 2
arxiv-2404-17189.description: Abstract We consider a cavity field state, which is created by the atom-cavity field’s interaction in the presence of a driven field. The two-level atom passes through the cavity and is driven by a weak classical field. A photon number dependent Stark shift is induced by the atom’s dispersive interaction with the cavity field.

arxiv-2410-17986.title: Federated Transformer: Multi-Party Vertical Federated Learning on Practical Fuzzily Linked Data
arxiv-2410-17986.creator: Zhaomin Wu, Junyi Hou, Yiqun Diao, Bingsheng He
arxiv-2410-17986.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) is an evolving paradigm that enables multiple parties to collaboratively train models without sharing raw data. Among its variants, Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) is particularly relevant in real-world, cross-organizational collaborations, where distinct features of a shared instance group are contributed by different parties.

arxiv-2602-09133.title: Uniting Iteration Limits for Mixed-Integer Quadratic MPC
arxiv-2602-09133.creator: Luke Fina, Christopher Petersen
arxiv-2602-09133.description: Abstract Iteration limited model predictive control (MPC) can stabilize a feedback control system under sufficient conditions; this work explores combining a low iteration limit MPC with a high iteration limit MPC for mixed-integer quadratic programs (MIQPs) where the suboptimality is due to solver iteration limits.

pmc-10597322.title: Novel side chain functionalized polystyrene/O-PBI blends with high alkaline stability for anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE)†
pmc-10597322.creator: Linus Hager, Manuel Hegelheimer, Julian Stonawski, Anna T. S. Freiberg, Camilo Jaramillo-Hernández, Gonzalo Abellán, Andreas Hutzler, Thomas Böhm, Simon Thiele, Jochen Kerres
pmc-10597322.description: We report the synthesis of a polystyrene-based anion exchange polymer bearing the cationic charge at a C6-spacer. The polymer is prepared by a functionalized monomer strategy. First, a copper halide catalyzed C–C coupling reaction between a styryl Grignard and 1,6-dibromohexane is applied, followed by quaternization with N-methylpiperidine and free radical polymerization.

pmc-11477946.title: The Adsorption of Chlorpromazine on the Surface of Gold Nanoparticles and Its Effect on the Toxicity to Selected Mammalian Cells
pmc-11477946.creator: Magdalena Oćwieja, Anna Barbasz, Oliwia Kowalska, Julia Maciejewska-Prończuk, Agata Lada, Bożena Czech
pmc-11477946.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Chlorpromazine (CPZ) is a first-generation neuroleptic with well-established antitumor and antiviral properties. Currently, numerous studies are focused on developing new methods for CPZ delivery; however, the knowledge regarding its conjugates with metal nanoparticles remains limited.

pmc-11512250.creator: Lucas Yago Melo Ferreira, Anderson Gonçalves de Sousa, Joannan Lima Silva, João Pedro Nunes Santos, David Gabriel do Nascimento Souza, Lixsy Celeste Bernardez Orellana, Sabrina Ferreira de Santana, Lara Beatriz Correia Moreira de Vasconcelos, Anibal Ramadan Oliveira, Eric Roberto Guimarães Rocha Agu
pmc-11512250.description: Agricultural pests can cause direct damage to crops, including chlorosis, loss of vigor, defoliation, and wilting. In addition, they can also indirectly damage plants, such as by transmitting pathogenic micro-organisms while feeding on plant tissues, affecting the productivity and quality of crops and interfering with agricultural production.

pmc-11643280.title: Law and Order of Colloidal Tectonics: From Molecules to Self-Assembled Colloids
pmc-11643280.creator: Loïc Leclercq
pmc-11643280.description: Since biochemists and biologists have progressed in understanding the mechanisms involved in living organisms, biological systems have become a source of inspiration for chemists. In this context, the concept of colloidal tectonics, describing the spontaneous formation of colloidal particles or supracolloidal structures in which the building blocks are called “tectons”, has emerged.

pmc-11713664.title: The association between tau pathology and later stages of memory processing is mediated by medial temporal lobe atrophy in typical Alzheimer's Disease
pmc-11713664.creator: Anika Wuestefeld, Salena Cui, Sandhitsu R Das, Long Xie, Emily McGrew, Paul A Yushkevich, Laura Wisse, David A Wolk
pmc-11713664.description: BackgroundTau pathology is closely related to cognitive decline in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Neurodegeneration is the putative mechanism by which tau leads to cognitive deficits. However, there is limited work on the associations between tau, neurodegeneration, and specific cognitive domains. We investigate potential mediating effects of medial temporal lobe (MTL) and neocortical neurodegeneration for different cognitive domains in amyloid‐ß‐positive (Aß+) adults.

pmc-12429199.title: Empowering Early Recovery: The Role of Impella 5.5 in Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Complicated by Cardiogenic Shock
pmc-12429199.creator: Aarti Desai, Jose Ruiz, Anna Shapiro, Rebecca Klingbeil, Archer Martin, Rohan Goswami
pmc-12429199.description: Introduction: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TCM), also known as stress cardiomyopathy or Broken Heart Syndrome, is a reversible, transient state of myocardial dyskinesis and apical ballooning. Infrequently, TCM may progress to severe life-threatening complications such as cardiogenic shock. Early mechanical circulatory support (MCS) is crucial to myocardial recovery in these cases.

pmc-12539298.title: Case Report: Presumed non-septic erosive sacroiliitis in a juvenile Bernese Mountain Dog: a 1.5-year follow-up
pmc-12539298.creator: Johanna Mäkitaipale, Nele Eley
pmc-12539298.description: A four-month-old intact male Bernese Mountain Dog was presented for an orthopedic examination due to an abnormal hind limb gait and tarsal hyperextension for the past 2 weeks. Pain was observed upon palpation of the lumbosacral region. Moderate bilateral tarsal hyperextension and mild metatarsal outward rotation were observed.

pmc-12652744.title: Prevalence of Torque Teno Virus (TTV) in Cervical Precursor Lesions and Cancer in Chilean Women
pmc-12652744.creator: Matías Guzmán-Venegas, Carolina Moreno-León, Cristian Andrade-Madrigal, Alejandra Román, Rancés Blanco, Iván Gallegos, Francisco Aguayo, Nabiha Yusuf
pmc-12652744.description: Torque teno virus (TTV) is a highly prevalent DNA virus in humans, but its role in carcinogenesis is not well understood. While human papillomavirus (HPV) is a well-established etiological agent in cervical cancer, co-infections with other viruses such as Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) or TTV may influence disease progression.

pmc-13234338.title: Rational design of a modular mRNA vaccine platform for rapid adaptation to SARS-CoV-2 variants
pmc-13234338.creator: Julia Rudert, Julia Volckmar, Andreas Jeron, Maike Bälkner, Pia Grimpe, Henning Jacobsen, Dandan Zhang, Giovana Bavia Bampi, Luka Cicin-Sain, Dunja Bruder, Joseph Rosenecker, Xiaoyan Ding
pmc-13234338.description: The ongoing emergence of novel SARS-CoV-2 variants due to viral mutations poses a persistent challenge to the efficacy of existing vaccines. To address this challenge, we engineered and comprehensively tested three optimized mRNA vaccine candidates, evaluating the kinetics, quality, and magnitude of antibody responses as well as antigen-specific T cell immunity during a prime-boost vaccination regimen in mice.

pmc-13383476.creator: Yueh-Ting Tsai, Bo-Yuan Wang, Sai-Wai Ho, Shun-Fa Yang, Yu-Hsun Wang, Chao-Bin Yeh, Ying-Cheng Chen
pmc-13383476.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThere is a limited body of research examining the association between long COVID and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) as well as all-cause mortality. This study aimed to investigate the association between long COVID and both MACE and mortality.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study utilized multicenter real-world data from the TriNetX research network platform, which contains electronic health records from multiple healthcare organizations. Patients aged 18 years and older who were diagnosed with COVID-19 between 2020 and 2023 were included.

pmc-13418420.title: In silico generation of gene expression profiles using diffusion models
pmc-13418420.creator: Alice Lacan, Romain André, Michèle Sebag, Blaise Hanczar
pmc-13418420.description: BackgroundRNA-seq data is used for precision medicine (e.g., cancer predictions), which benefits from deep learning approaches to analyze complex gene expression data. However, transcriptomics datasets often have few samples compared to deep learning standards. Synthetic data generation is thus being explored to address this data scarcity.

pmc-13425590.title: Atypical Autonomic‐Predominant Guillain‐Barré Syndrome With Pandysautonomia Mimicking Parkinsonism and Recurrent Syncope: A Case Report
pmc-13425590.creator: Rua Alsaeed, Nabel Rajab Basha, Sangharsha Thapa, Jin Li
pmc-13425590.description: Guillain‐Barré syndrome with pandysautonomia can mimic neurodegenerative and cardiogenic conditions, particularly in elderly patients presenting with autonomic symptoms and parkinsonian features. Timely neurologic evaluation and ganglioside antibody testing—especially anti‐GM2—are essential for accurate diagnosis and the initiation of immunotherapy, which may result in significant clinical improvement even in atypical, chronic presentations.

pmc-13535457.title: 2 Relationships Between Plasma KIM-1 Levels, Peripheral Immune Profiles and Disease-Free Survival Outcomes in the TransRAMPART Study
pmc-13535457.creator: James Jones, Rebecca Wray, Carla Castignani, Duncan McKenzie, Camilla Cucinotta, Carley Batley, Gemma Tsang-Pells, Helen Su, Sarah Welsh, Axel Bex, Paul Nathan, David Harrison, Tim Eisen, Max Emmerich, Samra Turajlic, Elena Frangou, Adam Laing, Angela Meade, Thomas Powles, James Larkin, Grant Stewar
pmc-13535457.description: BackgroundDespite optimal surgery, approximately 1 in 3 patients with renal cell carcinoma (RCC) will develop relapse.
